title: valley-floor
text:
A Python package for delineating valley floors from digital elevation models (DEMs).
Valley floors are the topographic region between valley walls shaped mainly by fluvial processes, composed of floodplains, terraces, alluvial fans, and channels.
The method combines two components:

Region growing — low-slope pixels connected to the channel network. Captures wider, unconfined valley floors with multiple channels and floodplains.
Reach flooding — reach-specific relative elevation thresholds derived from cross-section analysis. Captures narrow, confined valley floors bounded by steep hillslopes.



Core package:
pip install "valley-floor @ git+https://github.com/avkoehl/valley-floor.git"
With the optional preprocessing pipeline and example dataset (requires streamkit):
pip install "valley-floor[streamkit] @ git+https://github.com/avkoehl/valley-floor.git"



Basic usage:
from valley_floor import (
    Parameters, 
    PreProcessingParameters,
    PostProcessingParameters,
    delineate_from_dem_and_flowlines
)

# dem is an xarray.DataArray of elevation values
# flowlines is a gpd.GeoDataFrame of flowline geometries 
result = delineate_from_dem_and_flowlines(
    dem=dem,
    flowlines=flowlines,
    params=Parameters(),
    preprocessing_params=PreProcessingParameters(),
    postprocessing_params=PostProcessingParameters()
)



Install the package with development dependencies and register the package’s virtual environment as a Jupyter kernel:
git clone git@github.com:avkoehl/valley-floor.git
cd valley-floor
uv sync                        # core only
uv sync --extra streamkit --group dev  # include streamkit and development dependencies
uv run python -m ipykernel install --user --name valley-floor # register the package's virtual environment as a Jupyter kernel
Run tests with pytest:
uv run pytest -v
Build the documentation and preview it locally:
uv run quartodoc build
quarto preview

title: Example
text: This notebook demonstrates how to delineate valley floors using valley-floor.

title: Example
text:
Entry points
The package provides two entry points:

delineate_from_dem_and_flowlines — the full pipeline. Takes a DEM and flowlines and handles all intermediate steps internally using streamkit. This is the recommended starting point for most users.
delineate — the core algorithm only. Takes precomputed HAND, subbasins, and cross section points. Use this if you want to bring your own inputs computed from a different tool or workflow. See the API reference for details.

This notebook uses delineate_from_dem_and_flowlines. Both the sample data and this entry point require the streamkit optional dependency:
pip install "valley-floor[streamkit] @ git+https://github.com/avkoehl/valley-floor.git"

title: Example
text:
Load sample data
The sample data is a DEM and flowlines for a small watershed in California (HUC 1805000203). Data is downloaded on first use and cached locally.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from valley_floor import (
    Parameters,
    PreprocessingParameters,
    PostprocessingParameters,
    delineate_from_dem_and_flowlines,
)
from valley_floor.data import load_sample_data

dem, flowlines = load_sample_data()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
dem.plot(ax=ax, cmap='terrain', add_colorbar=True)
flowlines.plot(ax=ax, color='steelblue', linewidth=0.5)
ax.set_title('DEM and Flowlines')
ax.set_axis_off()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

title: Example
text:
Run delineation
Run the full pipeline with default parameters. Passing PostprocessingParameters applies postprocessing to the output — remove this argument to get the raw union of the two components.

result = delineate_from_dem_and_flowlines(
    dem,
    flowlines,
    params=Parameters(),
    preprocessing_params=PreprocessingParameters(),
    postprocessing_params=PostprocessingParameters(),
)

title: Example
text:
Visualize results

import numpy as np

valley_floor = result['valley_floor']
floor_masked = valley_floor.where(valley_floor == 1)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
dem.plot(ax=ax, cmap='terrain', add_colorbar=True, alpha=0.8)
floor_masked.plot(ax=ax, cmap='Reds', add_colorbar=False, alpha=0.6)
ax.set_title('Valley Floor')
ax.set_axis_off()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()









region_floor = result['region_floor']
flood_floor = result['flood_floor']

region_masked = region_floor.where(region_floor == 1)
flood_masked = flood_floor.where(flood_floor == 1)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 6))

dem.plot(ax=axes[0], cmap='terrain', add_colorbar=False, alpha=0.8)
region_masked.plot(ax=axes[0], cmap='Greens', add_colorbar=False, alpha=0.6)
axes[0].set_title('Region Growing Component')
axes[0].set_axis_off()

dem.plot(ax=axes[1], cmap='terrain', add_colorbar=False, alpha=0.8)
flood_masked.plot(ax=axes[1], cmap='Oranges', add_colorbar=False, alpha=0.6)
axes[1].set_title('Reach Flooding Component')
axes[1].set_axis_off()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

title: Parameters
text:
Parameters(
    region_smooth_radius=90,
    region_smooth_sigma=30,
    region_slope_threshold=3.0,
    region_dilation_radius=3,
    flood_steep_slope=10.0,
    flood_min_elevation_gain=10.0,
    flood_default_elevation=10,
    flood_percentile=85.0,
    flood_min_points=10,
)
Parameters for the core valley floor delineation algorithm.
Controls the region growing and reach flooding components. All spatial units are in the CRS units of the input DEM (typically meters).










Name
Type
Description




region_smooth_radius
int
Radius of the Gaussian smoothing kernel in meters, applied to the DEM before slope calculation in region growing.


region_smooth_sigma
int
Standard deviation of the Gaussian smoothing kernel in pixels.


region_slope_threshold
float
Maximum slope in degrees for a pixel to be included in the region growing component.


region_dilation_radius
int
Radius in pixels for dilating the channel network before region growing connectivity analysis.


flood_steep_slope
float
Minimum slope in degrees to identify a valley wall in cross section analysis.


flood_min_elevation_gain
float
Minimum elevation gain in meters for a steep segment to be considered a valley wall.


flood_default_elevation
int
Default HAND threshold in meters applied to reaches with insufficient cross section data.


flood_percentile
float
Percentile of slope break elevations used to derive the HAND threshold per reach.


flood_min_points
int
Minimum number of slope break points required to derive a reach threshold from data rather than the default.
